remediation.issue: Example credentials and tokens can be mistaken for real secrets.
remediation.suggestion: Use clearly fake placeholders such as YOUR_API_KEY and add a note that examples must not contain real secrets.

remediation.suggestion: Document that users should run the harness only against trusted local servers and reviewed commands.

content.user_title: Build MCP Servers for AI Tools
content.value_statement: Building reliable MCP servers requires protocol knowledge, secure API design, and strong evaluation practices. This skill provides structured guidance for planning, coding, testing, and improving MCP integrations.
actual_capabilities: Explains MCP server planning, naming, transport selection, and tool design.
Provides TypeScript and Python implementation patterns for MCP tools.
Shows how to validate inputs with Zod or Pydantic schemas.
Includes guidance for pagination, structured output, and error handling.
Supplies an evaluation workflow and scripts for testing MCP servers.
Links to protocol and SDK documentation that developers should review.
limitations: It is a development guide, not a complete server generator.
External API details must be supplied by the developer.
Evaluation scripts require a configured Anthropic API key.
Generated examples still need security review before deployment.

use_cases.title: Create a New MCP Integration
use_cases.description: Plan and implement an MCP server that exposes a product API through well-described tools.

use_cases.title: Improve Existing Tool Design
use_cases.description: Review tool names, schemas, response formats, and annotations for better agent usability.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Server Quality
use_cases.description: Create evaluation questions and run the included harness against an MCP server.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic MCP Server
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan an MCP server for this API: [describe service]. Identify core tools, naming patterns, transport choice, and required authentication.

prompt_templates.title: Design Tool Schemas
prompt_templates.prompt: Design MCP tool schemas for these operations: [list operations]. Include validation rules, response formats, pagination, and clear descriptions.

prompt_templates.title: Review an MCP Implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my MCP server implementation for protocol fit, input validation, error handling, response size, and security issues. Focus on actionable fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Create Evaluation Tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Create evaluation questions for this MCP server. Make them read-only, realistic, stable, independently verifiable, and difficult enough to test tool quality.

output_examples.input: A developer asks how to expose a task management API through MCP.
output_examples.output: A structured implementation plan with server naming, transport choice, tool list, schemas, authentication notes, and testing steps.

output_examples.input: A team provides an existing MCP tool with broad responses and weak validation.
output_examples.output: A focused review that recommends stricter schemas, pagination, safer error messages, and clearer tool descriptions.

output_examples.input: A QA engineer needs evaluation coverage for a new MCP server.
output_examples.output: A set of read-only evaluation scenarios with expected answers, verification guidance, and harness usage notes.

best_practices: Start with protocol and SDK documentation before writing server code.
Use strict input schemas and clear tool descriptions for every tool.
Evaluate with realistic read-only tasks before publishing the server.
anti_patterns: Do not expose every API endpoint without considering agent workflows.
Do not return unbounded data without pagination or truncation.
Do not place secrets in code, examples, logs, or tool responses.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you design, implement, test, and evaluate MCP servers for external services.

faq.question: Does it support TypeScript and Python?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for TypeScript MCP SDK patterns and Python FastMCP patterns.

faq.question: Does it generate a full MCP server automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture, examples, checklists, and evaluation support for developer-led implementation.

faq.question: Can it help with security design?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers input validation, authentication handling, safe errors, DNS rebinding protection, and command injection prevention.

faq.question: What tools are needed for evaluations?
faq.answer: The evaluation harness uses Python dependencies, an Anthropic API key, and access to the MCP server under test.

faq.question: Is it useful with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance works for Claude, Claude Code, and Codex workflows that create or review MCP servers.
